window.title: textgrid-to-Multi-Engine Label Converter
pipeline.audit.threshold.tooltip: Count issues per audio (too short / zero length / overlapping) and only flag files that reach this count.
pipeline.audit.min_ms.tooltip: Phonemes shorter than this count as one issue. Consonants/breaths in singing are often 20-40 ms; 20-30 is recommended.
pipeline.audit.ignore_silence.tooltip: Breaths and pauses are short by nature; when checked they are not counted as too-short.
pipeline.audit.hint: Scans the phones tier of the TextGrid next to each audio, counts issues, lists audios above the threshold and lets you delete them with their same-name files.
pipeline.audit.delete_hint: Only deletes audios found in the last scan; asks for confirmation first.
pipeline.audit.summary: Scanned {total} audios (checked {checked}, skipped without TextGrid {skipped}); {flagged} have issues ≥ {threshold}.
msg.err.audit_empty: Nothing to delete. Run the check first.
msg.confirm.audit_delete:
Delete {count} audio files and their selected same-name files?

This cannot be undone.
log.audit.start: Start check: issue threshold ≥ {threshold}, too-short {min_ms:g} ms
pipeline.tifa.title: Next: fine-grained labeling with TIFA
pipeline.tifa.desc: TIFA cannot handle very long audio, so the previous steps already split the audio at AP/SP and wrote a TextGrid, a .lab (pinyin) and a .txt (hanzi + pinyin) for every segment. Go to "2.TextGrid Infer → TIFA Infer" and use the segmented folder as input.
lab.asr.csv.tooltip: Column 1 path = audio or folder path (relative paths resolve against the CSV folder); column 2 title = optional title; column 3 lyrics = lyrics. When set, the CSV takes priority over the folder / selected files.
lab.asr.csv.template.tooltip: Choose where to save a template with English headers path,title,lyrics (UTF-8 BOM, opens cleanly in Excel)
lab.asr.csv.hint: Relative paths resolve against the CSV folder; a row pointing to a folder applies its lyrics to every audio in that folder
lab.asr.model_hint: Needs full HuggingFace weights (config.json + *.safetensors): Qwen3-ASR-1.7B and Qwen3-ForcedAligner-0.6B. A ModelScope cache folder also works (snapshots/<revision> is resolved automatically).
lab.asr.device.tooltip: Auto = CUDA when a GPU build of torch is available, otherwise CPU. Choosing CUDA in a CPU-only environment raises an error.
lab.asr.dtype.tooltip: Auto = bfloat16 on GPU (float16 when unsupported), float32 on CPU. Use float16 if VRAM is tight.
lab.asr.batch.tooltip: Passed to the official max_inference_batch_size (batching of internal chunks). Use 1 when VRAM is short.
lab.asr.chunk.tooltip: Run inference chunk by chunk to lower peak VRAM: audio is cut into chunks of about this length at quiet points, then text is joined and timestamps are shifted back. 30-60 s is recommended for 6 GB cards; 0 delegates chunking to the official code (180 s per chunk with timestamps, which often runs out of memory on long audio).
lab.asr.aligner_cpu.tooltip: Run the aligner in system memory so it does not use VRAM (recommended on 6 GB cards when both models are loaded; slower). Only applies to the ASR + align mode.
lab.asr.encoder_cpu.tooltip: Run the audio encoder (~0.3B) in system memory: saves about 0.6 GB of VRAM with identical output and almost no speed loss. Recommended on 6 GB cards.
lab.asr.skip_silence.tooltip: Detect speech spans by energy and only send those to the model, so interludes/silence no longer produce hallucinated text. Pauses shorter than 5 s are merged into the same span (treated as a normal breath); only gaps longer than 5 s are skipped. Threshold = max(-55 dBFS, peak-35 dB), so quiet breaths are usually kept.
lab.asr.engine_hint: Chunked execution: each chunk is inferred separately and the CUDA cache is released in between; timestamps are merged back onto the full track. If VRAM is still short, switch to ASR only and then align only as two steps.
lab.asr.lyrics.save.tooltip: Write the current lyrics to _lyrics.txt next to the audio (also saved when switching audio or starting recognition, and checked every 3 seconds)
lab.asr.lyrics.no_audio: Select an audio file in the list first
lab.asr.prompt.hint: Final prompt = system prompt + reference lyrics. Saved to {name}_lyrics.txt on "Save lyrics", on audio switch, on start, and every 3 seconds when edited; untouched files read {name}_lyrics.txt / .txt / .lrc in order.
lab.asr.run_mode.tooltip: ASR+align loads both models (most VRAM). ASR only skips the aligner and writes txt/lab. Align only loads just the aligner and reads the existing .txt (or .lab) to produce _ASR.json — useful to run the two stages separately when VRAM is short.
lab.wavname.title: Generate LAB from WAV name
lab.wavname.auto_sp.tooltip: On by default. When on, SP is only added at the head/tail; R in file names is kept as is
detect.title: Phoneme Check (Too Short)
detect.threshold.tooltip: Phonemes shorter than this value (ms) will be listed (regardless of name)
detect.ignore_edge_sp.tooltip: When checked, SP at the start/end of the tier is skipped; SP in the middle is still checked

textgrid.title: TextGrid Inference (Based on HubertFA)
textgrid.browse_files.tooltip: Multiple selection allowed; selected files take priority over the folder
textgrid.workers.tooltip: Split files across N parallel processes in DML/WebGPU mode (requires enough GPU memory)
textgrid.nonlex.tooltip: Off by default. When enabled, the phoneme sequence gets SP inserted at utterance start/end and between words so alignment can absorb silence; AP/EP come from the model's NLL detector and remaining gaps are filled with SP
ap.title: AP Labels (Breath Detection)
ap.out_hint: Leave empty to write next to the audio files; an existing TextGrid with the same name will be overwritten
ap.mode.new: Build new AP/SP labels (no TextGrid needed)
ap.mode.merge: Merge AP into an existing TextGrid (SP + empty intervals)
ap.mode.hint: New mode suits raw recordings; merge keeps the existing hanzi/words labels and splits SP and empty intervals into SP/AP
ap.other_mark.tooltip: Mark used for non-breath intervals in new mode (default V). Avoid SP: the splitter treats SP as silence too, so an all SP/AP tier gives no split points
msg.err.ap_params: Invalid AP parameters: threshold must be 0~1, min breath must be > 0, SP absorb must be >= 0
msg.err.ap_no_audio: No audio files found to process

2. Fixed ratio
3. Right ratio

mark.svdb.title: SVDB Generate
mark.svdb.recursive.tooltip: When checked, every subfolder containing json/word_phone.json and wav files is processed, at any depth; otherwise only the selected folder and its first-level subfolders. The "Generate TextGrid" button uses the same setting.
mark.svdb.generate_tg.tooltip: Convert the json data in the voicebank folder (and subfolders) back to TextGrid: word_phone.json -> words tier; when a dictionary is selected, words are split with it (tail ratio) into SV phones for the phones tier, otherwise ds_phone.json phones are used directly

textgrid.skip_penalty.tooltip: Cost of skipping a phoneme (zero duration); larger = less skipping

tifa.del_sp.tooltip: Run del_SP after inference to drop redundant or adjacent SP intervals (ignores AP,SP,EP)

other.json2tg.out_hint: Leave empty to write next to the JSON; output is named {audio}.TextGrid (the _Aligner / _ASR suffix is dropped)
other.json2tg.min_interval.tooltip: Words/chars with identical start and end (or too short) are extended to this duration (default 10 ms) so they are not dropped; following items shift accordingly
other.json2tg.min_interval.invalid: Invalid min interval: enter a value between 0 and 5000 ms
other.json2tg.no_files: No *_ASR.json / *_Aligner.json found. Check the folder or enable "Include subfolders".
mark.volume.out_hint: Leave empty to only detect without moving files; when set, filtered audio is moved into this folder (subfolder structure preserved, duplicate names get a suffix)
mark.volume.threshold.tooltip: RMS is computed in 50 ms frames and then averaged; below this value counts as too quiet. 0 dBFS is full scale (linear 1.0), lower is quieter
mark.volume.peak.tooltip: Maximum amplitude of the whole file. Reaching this value means the audio is not blank and will not be output; only files below BOTH thresholds are listed
mark.volume.hint: Average RMS = mean of 50 ms frame RMS values; peak = maximum amplitude. A file is treated as blank only when both are below their thresholds; when an output folder is set, matching files are moved there.

mark.splitlab.lab_ignore_enable.tooltip: Nothing is ignored by default; tick this to skip the marks on the right
mark.splitlab.out_hint: Leave empty to write into <wav folder>/segments
mark.splitlab.silences.tooltip: Comma or space separated (default SP,AP); **empty marks are also treated as split points**. Adjacent split ranges are merged and both neighbouring segments include that range
mark.splitlab.write_tg.tooltip: Write a TextGrid next to each audio segment (tiers are clipped at the split points and shifted to start at 0)
mark.splitlab.export_lab.tooltip: Write a .lab next to each segment from the words/phones tier (space separated pinyin/phonemes), ready for TIFA
mark.splitlab.export_txt.tooltip: Write a .txt next to each segment: first line hanzi, second line pinyin
mark.splitlab.export_hint: Segments without any lyric content are skipped
mark.splitlab.lab_out_hint: Leave empty to write next to the TextGrids
mark.splitlab.lab_ignore.tooltip: These marks are skipped in the lab (default AP,SP,EP,R)
mark.words.title: Rebuild words tier from phones
mark.words.out_hint: Leave empty to overwrite the original TextGrid files
mark.csv.title: Generate transcriptions.csv
mark.csv.tg_folder.tooltip: Leave empty to read the TextGrid next to each wav (song.wav → song.TextGrid); matching is by file name, also in recursive mode.
mark.csv.read_tiers: Read extra TextGrid tiers (words / notes / note_slur)
mark.csv.read_tiers.tooltip: If a words tier exists, generate ph_num/word_seq; a notes tier generates note_seq/note_dur; a note_slur tier generates note_slur
mark.csv.recursive.tooltip: Also scan subfolders (multi-pitch); sample names get a folder prefix (e.g. A4_01) to avoid collisions
mark.csv2tg.title: CSV to TextGrid
mark.csv2tg.out_hint: Leave empty to write next to the CSV
mark.csv2tg.hint: Tiers: words / phones / ph-num / notes / note-slur (no underscores, no spaces); the ph-num tier is always written when ph_num exists (mark = phone count of the group), output <name>.TextGrid. Without a dictionary the words tier is skipped (a dictionary rebuilds it exactly like "Rebuild words from phones")
mark.phnum.title: Add ph_num
mark.phnum.preset.tooltip: Quickly pick a preset C+V set from tg2svdb/cv_dicts; selecting one switches to 'vowels + consonants' and fills both paths
mark.phnum.hint: Grouping: a vowel (or a run of vowels forming one final) plus the consonants right after it form one group; a bare vowel is its own group. Write one final per line in the vowel file - a line with several phonemes (e.g. iU N) means they are one compound final.
mark.game.title: GAME MIDI
mark.game.max_chunk.tooltip: Default 30 s; 0 = no chunking. Audio is split at word boundaries (preferring unvoiced phonemes). Lower to 8-16 s if VRAM is insufficient (medium 30 s peaks at ~4.4 GB).
mark.game.workers.tooltip: Number of audio files processed concurrently. 1 = sequential. Use 2-4 on CPU (threads share one model).
mark.game.workers.tooltip_gpu: Number of audio files processed concurrently. A DirectML session cannot run concurrently (it crashes), so parallelism uses that many PROCESSES, each loading its own copy of the model: VRAM is about N times a single instance. Use 2-3; lower 'Max chunk' first if VRAM runs out.
